title: Replay lane consent and tiered recovery options for affected tenants
body:
Status draft for customer outreach: replay consent & tiered recovery lanes

TL;DR
We experienced a multi-region KV-cache synchronization fault on 2027-02-01 that caused increased latency and some duplicated/partial token sequences for a subset of inference requests routed through the EU and US routing planes between 01:03–02:42 UTC. The platform has been stabilized; we are offering customers a set of recovery options (including an opt-in replay path) so you can choose the remediation that best fits your data-safety and product-experience needs.

Primary impact summary (concise)
- Window: 2027-02-01 01:03:12 UTC — 2027-02-01 02:42:09 UTC (mitigated and routing corrected at 02:42)
- Affected tenants: approx. 2.4% of active tenants with cross-region requests during window
- Observed symptoms: elevated tail latency (p95–p999), occasional duplicated tokens or truncated structured outputs in streaming mode, rare ordering anomalies for multi-message sessions
- No customer payload data was modified or lost by Redwood; root cause relates to cache state divergence and subsequent stale-KV read paths

What happened (short technical narrative for customers)
- Our KV caching layer used to accelerate autoregressive generation experienced a race when a regional cache invalidation coincided with a concurrent warm-start request.
- Under high concurrency a small percentage of requests read partially stale KV state, producing longer token generation times and occasionally producing redundant token fragments on the stream.
- The routing control plane fell back to a compatible model variant in a few zones to preserve availability; that fallback reduced throughput and contributed to visible latency spikes for some tenants.

What we did (timeline & mitigations)
- 01:05 UTC: SRE alerted via observability triggers (p999 latency, streaming error rate)
- 01:12 UTC: Auto-fallback engaged for affected zones to maintain correctness for new requests (routing to model-variant B)
- 01:40 UTC: Hotfix deployed to prevent concurrent invalidation/warm-start races (patch applied to cache write-locking and prefetch scheduling)
- 02:42 UTC: Routing control plane fully stabilized; traffic returned to normal paths
- 02/01–02/02: Post-fix validation, replay tool verification and integrity checks run across sample workloads

Customer-facing remediation options (choose one)
We want customers to control whether and how their historical requests during the window are reprocessed. We are offering three lanes you can select from depending on your risk tolerance and product needs. Each lane includes clear guarantees and expected timelines.

Lane A — System-automated replay (recommended for conversational products that want seamless correction)
- Redwood will reprocess affected requests on your behalf, using the same model revision that served the original request unless you opt to change it.
- We will ensure deterministic inputs (prompt + context snapshot) and attach a replay provenance header to outputs for auditability.
- Expected time to completion: 24–72 hours after opt-in closes
- Guarantee: we will surface a verification delta report (per-tenant) highlighting changed outputs and potential user-visible deltas.
- Data handling: we only read stored request traces needed for replay; no external customer data is exported.

Lane B — Manual replay with review (recommended for high-sensitivity customers)
- We provide a downloadable replay package (batched requests + checksums) and a self-serve runner you can execute in your private deployment or via our dedicated environment.
- Redwood SREs will offer a one-time observability session to help interpret diffs and verify integrity.
- Expected support window: we will retain replay packages for 14 days from generation request.

Lane C — No replay; credit & monitoring (recommended for customers who prefer no reprocessing)
- If you opt out of replay, we will issue a service credit proportional to estimated affected units and extend elevated monitoring for 30 days for your tenant routes.
- No replay artifacts will be retained beyond immediate verification.

How to choose / timeline for opt-in
- Opt-in period opens: 2027-02-03 09:00 UTC
- Opt-in period closes: 2027-02-10 09:00 UTC (if we do not receive a choice, we will default to Lane C: No replay with credit after final outreach)
- To choose: customers may select their lane via the Customer Console -> Incidents -> 2027-02-01 KV-cache divergence or reply to this communication with a ticket link (CS-8721) and the chosen lane.

Integrity & privacy assurances
- All replayed executions are performed in the same security boundary as original inference and under the tenant's existing encryption/KMS policies.
- We will attach audit metadata (original request id, replay id, replay timestamp) to outputs and provide a delta checksum to help you reconcile changed outputs.
- Replays will not trigger new downstream billing beyond a capped reconciliation credit; billing adjustments are detailed in the credit terms below.

Credit & billing notes (summary)
- If you select Lane A or B and results materially change user-visible outputs, Redwood will apply a one-time adjustment credit to offset replay compute unless you explicitly ask to pay for the reprocessed units.
- If you select Lane C we will apply a fixed credit based on estimated affected tokens (details provided per-tenant)

Risk matrix / caveats
- Replays may produce different text due to non-determinism in sampling-based decoding; for deterministic models / temperature=0 variants we expect high fidelity to original outputs.
- For stateful session products, replays may not perfectly reconstitute external side-effects (webhooks, third-party calls) — customers relying on external side-effects should prefer manual review (Lane B) or pay to re-run through their own environment.

Customer-facing verification deliverables
- Per-tenant delta report: list of reprocessed request ids, original vs replay token count, checksum diff, example deltas (up to 25 rows)
- Integrity assertion: signed JSON summary proving replay inputs and outputs with timestamps and operator id
- Optional: side-by-side sample replay recordings for up to 3 customer-provided test sessions

Notes to internal teams (for CS authors & SRE)
- CS playbook: send initial choice email to tenants with >0.1% request error rate during window; for others send opt-in summary tile in Console only
- SRE: ensure replay-runner uses patched cache semantics and same model weights used for original request unless customer requests model-change review
- Legal: coordinate with customers on any replay that involves PII-sensitive prompts; require explicit documented consent for replays that surface raw user data in logs

Draft status page blurb (short)
- We investigated a regional cache synchronization issue that affected a subset of requests on 2027-02-01. The platform has been stabilized; customers can choose a replay or credit option to remediate any user-visible anomalies. Full customer instructions and opt-in form available in the Console and in your assigned CS ticket.

Suggested customer email subject lines (A/B test)
- "Action required: Choose a recovery path for requests impacted on 2027-02-01"
- "Redwood: Options to reconcile inference results from 2027-02-01 incident"

Open questions before final send
- Confirm final credit calculation method with finance (link to CS-credits doc)
- Confirm retention window for replay packages (SRE proposes 14 days, CS prefers 30)
- Does privacy/legal require opt-in for all EU tenants regardless of lane? (regulatory check needed)

Next steps (internal)
- 2027-02-02 15:00 UTC: Internal dry-run of delta report generation (owner: Jordan Kim)
- 2027-02-02 18:00 UTC: Legal sign-off on consent copy (owner: Ava Patel)
- 2027-02-03 08:00 UTC: Send initial CTA to affected tenant owners (owner: Riley Martinez)

Contact
- Primary CS contact: Riley Martinez (riley@redwood.ai)
- SRE escalation: oncall@sre.redwood.ai
- Product escalation (if model-change requested): Marcus Li

---
Notes to self: make the Console CTA a one-click lane chooser + require SLA acknowledgement for lane A automated replays. Need UX: visible delta report link in Console and option to download full replay package.
